metadata.note: The Bangor and Piscataquis Railroad (first train Dec 1869, Old Town – Dover and Foxcroft; Guilford 1871; Abbot c.1874; Blanchard 1877; Greenville Jul 14 1884) and the Bangor and Katahdin Iron Works Railway (Milo Junction – Katahdin Iron Works, 1882), drawn through each of their operators: the B&P itself (1869-1872 and 1877-1891), the European and North American Railway, which operated the B&P under lease 1873-1876, the B&KIW (1882-1886, then leased to the B&P from Jul 1 1887), and the Bangor and Aroostook from the Apr 1 1892 lease of both. Segment years are inclusive (app.js coversYear), so each handover year belongs to the incoming operator only: B&P to 1872 / E&NA from 1873; E&NA to 1876 / B&P from 1877; B&KIW to 1886 / B&P from 1887; B&P to 1891 / BAR from 1892. Bangor – Old Town was E&NA (later Maine Central) track and is drawn under its owner in european_north_american_danforth.geojson, not here. The 2 ft gauge Monson Railroad (Monson Junction – Monson, 1883-1943) was a separate company and is not drawn. Nothing freight-only is drawn: the KIW rails left in place 1922-1933 are excluded (Rule 1). Steam from the start; no horsecar years (Rule 5). Built to 5 ft 6 in gauge as far as Abbot; regauged 1877.

not_yet_sourced: Whether B&P trains ran through to Bangor over the E&NA / Maine Central, or passengers changed at Old Town, is unknown for 1869-1892 (likely through-running under E&NA operation 1873-1876, but unproven). Nothing B&P-coloured is drawn south of Old Town either way.
The first-train day Dec 14 1869 is not in Poor's Manual (which gives December 1869) and is unverified; the year is firm.
Abbot opening: 1873 (Poor's 1878-1887, 'on the completion ... to Abbot, in 1873') vs December 1874 (Poor's 1885/1887 opening list). Drawn from 1875 under the E&NA.
Blanchard opening: 1875 (Poor's 1878, 1879) vs May 1877 (Poor's 1880, 1884, 1885, 1887). Drawn from 1877; the 1876 Pathfinder still shows Abbot as the terminus.
B&KIW: the first 6 miles opened Dec 1881, but no source says passenger trains ran in 1881. Drawn from 1882.
E&NA lease start: Dec 1 1872 (Poor's 1876-77 consolidation date) vs 1873 (later editions). Drawn E&NA from 1873, consistent with both.
Exact day of the 1877 regauging to standard gauge.

Greenville Branch end: drawn to 1961 on the assumption that it ended with the BAR's last passenger trains (Sep 4 1961). The last positively confirmed year is 1951, from the Feb 1952 Official Guide's mixed train Derby – Greenville.
Old Town – South Lagrange end: last confirmed 1929 (Fowler, 1929 BAR timetable); gone by 1939. Drawn to 1929, the last confirmed year, not a known end. 1934 is an unsourced guess.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout; only the B&KIW headway is loosely derived (FY1883 passenger train-miles).

segments.note: Opened Old Town – Dover and Foxcroft in December 1869 (Poor's Manual 1873-74: 'Opened from Old Town to Foxcroft, December, 1869'; Poor's 1885 and 1887: 'to Dover in December, 1869'). Built to 5 ft 6 in gauge to match the E&NA at Old Town. Operated by the B&P itself to the end of 1872: 36,450 passengers in calendar 1872, 4 locomotives and 2 passenger cars (Poor's 1873-74). The often-quoted day, Dec 14 1869, is not in Poor's and is unverified. Passengers for Bangor changed to, or ran over, the European and North American at Old Town — which of the two is unresolved; Bangor – Old Town is E&NA track and is drawn under that company. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced: no B&P public timetable was found; it assumes one to two trains each way a day, which fits the 2-5 passenger cars Poor's reports.
sources: Segment-level: the note's dates and traffic come from Poor's Manual 1873-74 and 1885/1887 opening lists, read in the 2026-10-08 B&P research report.

segments.note: B&P operation resumed Dec 1 1876, when the E&NA defaulted on the Oct 1 1876 rental and the stockholders 'resumed possession' (Poor's 1878); the B&P reports its own operating statistics from FY to Sep 30 1877 (17,164 passenger train-miles) and 46,692 passengers in FY1886 (Poor's 1887). Regauged to standard gauge in 1877 (by Sep 30 1877, Poor's 1878; exact day unknown). Ends 1891 because the line was leased to the Bangor and Aroostook from Apr 1 1892, drawn from 1892 as the BAR. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not sourced: no B&P public timetable was found; it assumes one to two trains each way a day, which fits the 2-5 passenger cars Poor's reports.
sources: Segment-level: the note's dates come from Poor's Manual 1878, 1887 and the 1898 Maine Railroad Commissioners' report (BAR lease dated Apr 1 1892), read in the 2026-10-08 B&P research report.

segments.note: BAR-operated from the Apr 1 1892 lease of the Bangor and Piscataquis. Until Nov 1905 this was the BAR's main route to Bangor, its trains running over the Maine Central from Old Town (Fowler line 21: 'Main line service operated over MEC from Bangor to Oldtown prior to opening of line from Northern Maine Junction'); after 1905 a branch. Pea Cove and Alton appear in the BAR public timetables of 1915 and 1929 but are gone from 1939 (Fowler letters). 1929 is the LAST CONFIRMED year, not a known end — service stopped some time between 1929 and 1939, and no source dates it. The '1934' sometimes given is a guess. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min is an ESTIMATE: two or three trains each way in the main-line years, fewer as a branch.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Apr 1 1892 lease (1898 Maine Railroad Commissioners' report); last confirmed year from Fowler line 21 station letters (1929 BAR timetable present, 1939 absent), per the BAR research report block [3].

Pieces: Derby – Dover-Foxcroft 12.7 mi traced vs 12.9 mi (Fowler MP 36.3 – 49.2). OSM abandoned grade tagged old_railway_operator=B&A (River Road and unnamed railway=abandoned ways). | Dover-Foxcroft – Guilford 8.2 mi traced vs 8.2 mi (Fowler MP 49.2 – 57.4). About 4.7 mi on the OSM B&A grade (the 'Bangor & Aroostook' footway, Johnson Road, Dover-Foxcroft Recreational Rail Trail) and 3.4 mi on the OpenHistoricalMap 'Bangor and Piscatquis Railroad' way where OSM has no grade (Sangerville – Guilford). The parallel MEC Newport/Dover-Foxcroft Rail Trail was avoided. | Guilford – Abbot Village 3.4 mi traced vs 3.3 mi (Fowler MP 57.4 – 60.7). OSM B&A grade ('Bangor & Aroostook' footway) with 0.8 mi of OpenHistoricalMap at Guilford. | Abbot Village – Blanchard 9.2 mi traced vs 10.7 mi (Fowler MP 60.7 – 71.4). OSM B&A grade (footways, Monson Junction Lane, unnamed tracks, Game Road). The Blanchard cut is placed at the line's nearest point to the Blanchard hamlet (0.9 km from it), which falls 1.1 mi short of Fowler's milepost; the milepost point would sit 2.0 km from the hamlet. The conservative cut was chosen so that this 1877 feature cannot claim track that may only have opened in 1884. Abbot Village – Blanchard + Blanchard – Greenville together trace 24.2 mi against 24.3 documented, so the error is in where the station falls, not in the line. | Blanchard – Greenville 15.1 mi traced vs 13.6 mi (Fowler MP 71.4 – 85.0) / 13.7 mi (Poor's 1885) — about 1.4 mi long because the Blanchard cut is placed conservatively (see the Abbot – Blanchard piece). OSM B&A grade (B And A Railroad South/North Road, Railroad Bed Road, B&A Railroad Road North, Dyer Road, Depot Street) with 0.5 mi of OpenHistoricalMap 'Greenville Branch' at the lake end. Ends at the West Cove / Greenville Junction terminus on Moosehead Lake.

segments.note: Derby – Dover-Foxcroft – Guilford – Abbot Village – Monson Junction – Blanchard – Greenville Junction, the ex-Bangor and Piscataquis main line, BAR-operated from the Apr 1 1892 lease. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 6) shows trains 9 and 12 Bangor – Dover-Foxcroft – Greenville, 'daily, except Sunday, MIXED TRAIN between Derby and Greenville' — a mixed train, which counts as passenger service. The 1961 end is APPROXIMATE: it assumes the branch's service ended with the BAR's last passenger trains on Sep 4 1961, which no source states for this branch; 1951 (the Feb 1952 Guide) is the last year positively confirmed. Line dismantled 1962-64. headway_min is an ESTIMATE; in 1951-52 it was one train each way a day except Sunday.
sources: Segment-level: the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 6 mixed-train footnote; start from the Apr 1 1892 lease (1898 Maine Railroad Commissioners' report); end assumed per the BAR research report block [12].
